Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then use the required fish-control bookshelf and wake-visual inspection skill before touching the policy. After that I’ll trace the assigned parent and sampled rollout evidence, implement exactly one candidate, and update both required evidence records.

The workspace confirms two mandatory pre-edit gates: compare the combined top-down/3D wake sheets against metrics, and document the diagnosis before changing the solver. I’m now identifying the best sampled trajectory and the most informative contrasting run, while also checking the inherited parent guidance and optimizer history for stagnation or prior mechanisms.

The visual comparison shows both the strongest and weakest sampled captures are genuinely self-propelled: each develops a sustained alternating mid-plane street and compact bilateral 3D structures through target approach, with no prewarm/advection artifact or wake collapse. Since every current sample captures, the useful contrast is score/arrival and actuation—not termination class. I’m resolving which controller variants produced those four captures and whether the assigned parent’s anterior-transfer mechanism is now independently supported.

The evidence resolves the parent mechanism clearly: anterior transfer achieved capture at `18.7495T` with the wake intact, but it was slower than both baseline samples (`18.2050T`, `18.6010T`) and did not improve clipping, speed-limit residence, force, or yaw-moment metrics. That makes it a safe mechanism demonstration, not an evidence-backed improvement to retain unchanged. I’m consulting the bookshelf now for a genuinely different feedback mechanism; any source-derived invariant will be recorded in the required structured block.

The new candidate will use one distinct mechanism: clipping-recovery steering allocation. It keeps the repeat-supported carrier, route, release, reserve, and total steering share, but transfers only the portion of tail steering that the current raw command predicts will be lost to same-direction saturation—and only when the anterior raw command has room to realize it. This directly addresses why the parent’s unconditional anterior transfer preserved capture yet improved neither actuation nor arrival. I’m recording the visual diagnosis and falsification boundary now, before editing the policy.

The solver now contains exactly one candidate with clipping-recovery allocation; no carrier, cadence, route, or release gains changed. I’m distilling the parent result into durable guidance next: unconditional spatial transfer is not supported as an improvement, while any further allocation test must be conditioned on actual instantaneous actuator feasibility and judged by repeatable arrival—not clamp reduction alone.

Both required evidence files are materially updated, and the candidate remains non-empty. Per the workspace contract, I’m invoking the dedicated checker now to validate guidance inheritance, policy/schema structure, and workspace boundaries without running CFD.

The checker passed the workspace boundary but found the same rendered metadata defect seen in the inherited run: `README.md` marks the identical guidance parent twice, so provenance cannot be resolved uniquely. I’ll remove only the duplicate marker, then rerun the checker. Julia is absent from `PATH`; I’ll also check the workspace’s configured checker instructions and available local toolchains before treating that as an environment limitation.

After the provenance repair, the semantic guidance check and workspace boundary check both pass. The remaining official runtime check is unavailable because no Julia executable exists in the searched system or workspace environments; while the checker reruns, I’m completing deterministic schema and structural checks so that limitation is isolated rather than masking a policy-field error.

A recorded-trace replay caught an important flaw before handoff: same-direction tail steering was never the component clipped in any of the four sampled trajectories, so the first allocator would be behaviorally inert on the available evidence. I’m treating that as falsification, not forcing the mechanism through a threshold. I’ll revise the candidate to a parameter-free normalized actuator-burden gate that uses the parent’s demonstrated safe spatial transfer only when the tail is more burdened than the head, then update the notes and durable lesson accordingly.

The inert proposal is removed. The final candidate now has a behaviorally selective burden allocator: recorded-trace replay activates it on roughly `10–13%` of terminal rows, never outside `4L`, with zero transfer when the head has no normalized envelope. I’ve updated both notes and durable guidance to include the rejected inert idea and the narrower mechanism; I’m rerunning the official checks on this final state.

Implemented exactly one 3D candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:347): normalized actuator-burden steering allocation preserving carrier and total steering authority.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:46): visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer block, falsification criteria, and recorded-trace selectivity check.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:181): evidence-backed negative lesson against unconditional anterior transfer.

Validation:

- Guidance semantic check: PASS
- Workspace boundary check: PASS
- Parameter-schema and delimiter checks: PASS
- Julia runtime check: unavailable because Julia is not installed
- CFD was not run, per contract.
